newsitem.title: UK: Hardy Oil says suspends well for appraisal.
newsitem.headline: Hardy Oil says suspends well for appraisal.

text.p: Hardy Oil & Gas said on Tuesday that it had suspended a well off Western Australia as a possible producer to consider an appraisal programme to assess its reserves and commercial potential.

Hardy said the well on the block WA 234P in the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia had tested oil at a stabilised rate of 7,600 barrels per day from a four metre interval between depths of 2,529.5 and 2,533.5 metres.
The company said the oil had a gravity of 48.5 metres API and occurred with minor quantities of gas.
Following a recent agreement with current operator Mobil, Hardy will earn a 30 percent interest in the block and would become its operator after completion.
Apart from Mobil, Hardy Oil's other partners in the well are PanCanadian and Tap Oil.
Hardy said it was continuing its exploration programme in ZOC-A 95-18 in the Timor Sea in which it has a 13 percent interest.
The exploration well is expected to be completed in two to three months.

Hardy has also confirmed that it had secured a 30 percent working interest in gazettal block AC96-4, which covers about 1,500 square km in the Timor Sea. Hardy's other partners in the block are Asamera with 30 percent and Coastal Oil & Gas Corporation with 40 percent.
